dhpak2.1:2.1: Changed the story title from Udena to Sāmāvatī.
dhpak2.1:11.1: The hatthiliṅgasakuṇo is a kind of large bird; the Pāli says nothing about a bill the size of an elephant's trunk. That description was removed.
dhpak2.1:19.3: sayaṃjātasāliṃ is rice growing of itself, not rice grown in the ascetic's own field.
dhpak2.1:23.3: Added the third day's elephant-lute instruction, which the English had omitted.
dhpak2.1:24.3: In the message about Udena's birth, maṃ sagabbhaṃ ... ānesī says the bird carried his pregnant mother, not Udena himself.
dhpak2.1:28.1: Changed the famine country from Ajita to Allakappa.
dhpak2.1:31.6: Added the child's death on the road (Puttopi antarāmagge mato hoti) after Kotūhalaka retrieved him.
dhpak2.1:42.4: Tenevassa ‘ghosakadevaputto’ti nāmaṃ ahosi names the deva son Ghosaka because of his far-carrying voice; the English had omitted the naming.
dhpak2.1:75.2: The wife's rebirth follows tassānubhāvena, the power of that gift of rice, not a claim about the Paccekabuddha's supernatural power.
dhpak2.1:93.1: Ghosaka's bhāriyaṃ vata kammaṃ expresses the gravity of what happened; it does not describe his own presumption.
dhpak2.1:96.1: vijātamātuyāpi amanāpā says the famished travelers would be displeasing even to the mother who bore them, not discourteous to her.
dhpak2.1:107.3: The court identifies Sāmāvatī as Ghosakaseṭṭhino dhītā, Ghosaka's daughter by adoption, not Bhaddavatiya's daughter.
dhpak2.1:107.6: Ghosaka feared the girls might be beaten, maltreated, and dragged away (kumārikānaṃ pothetvā viheṭhetvā kaḍḍhanabhayena).
dhpak2.1:118.3: Nālāgiri's range, vīsati yojanasataṃ, is twenty hundred leagues (2,000), not 120.
dhpak2.1:121.5: Udena's later wish for five conveyances has the corresponding ...satavīsasata... and was corrected to 2,000 leagues.
dhpak2.1:125.5: Udena first drops the kahāpaṇapasibbakaṃ, a sack of coins; the denomination is unspecified.
dhpak2.1:125.6: He then drops the suvaṇṇapasibbakaṃ, a sack of gold; the final delay is for gold, not silver.
dhpak2.1:142.3: The tree deity cannot be oramattikā, insignificant; the former English ‘mundane’ changed the sense.
dhpak2.1:144.5: The hungry laborer, sahasā abhuñjitvāva, did not eat immediately. The former English made his hunger spoken and his refusal sudden.
dhpak2.1:147.5: The ascetics ask the tree deity buddhoti vadesi (‘Did you say “Buddha”?’); this is a question, not an instruction.
dhpak2.1:155.8: After Khujjuttarā teaches, tā sabbāpi sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahiṃsu says all five hundred women attain Stream-entry; the English had omitted this.
dhpak2.1:162.1: In Dhp 322, assatarā are mules, not horses; the Sindh horses are a separate item in the verse.
dhpak2.1:165.3: The live cocks were handed to the page by Māgandiyā's uncle (tena dinne), not by Māgandiyā.
dhpak2.1:182.2: The five hundred uttarāsaṅgā are upper robes. The Pāli does not specify that they were yellow.
dhpak2.1:184.1: Corrected the values, lot sizes, and frequencies of Ānanda's robe gifts.
dhpak2.1:190.2: The women died anipphalā, with spiritual fruit from their attainments. The former English turned this into the fruit of past deeds.
dhpak2.1:193.2: The king was gehaṃ nibbāpento, extinguishing the house, when he sat down; the English had said he had already extinguished it.
dhpak2.1:198.8: The Paccekabuddha's pyre was lit; the Pāli does not mention oil.
dhpak2.1:199.3: The Pāli says a thousand cartloads of firewood could not make the absorbed Paccekabuddha feel the heat.
